The proposed solution correctly computes the quantum Fisher metric for a pure state in the Madelung representation:

1. Expressing the spatial derivative of the wavefunction $\psi = \sqrt{\mathcal{P}}e^{iS/\hbar}$ in terms of the osmotic velocity $u_\mu = \frac{\hbar}{2m}\partial_\mu \ln\mathcal{P}$ and current velocity $\pi_\mu = \frac{1}{m}\partial_\mu S$:
   $$\partial_\mu \psi = \frac{m}{\hbar}\sqrt{\mathcal{P}}(u_\mu + i\pi_\mu)e^{iS/\hbar}$$

2. Computing the inner product and connection term:
   $$\operatorname{Re}\langle\partial_\mu\psi|\partial_\nu\psi\rangle = \frac{m^2}{\hbar^2}\langle u_\mu u_\nu + \pi_\mu\pi_\nu\rangle_{\mathcal{P}}$$
   $$\langle\psi|\partial_\mu\psi\rangle = i\frac{m}{\hbar}\langle\pi_\mu\rangle_{\mathcal{P}} \quad (\text{since } \langle u_\mu\rangle_{\mathcal{P}} = 0)$$

3. The symmetric logarithmic derivative (SLD) quantum Fisher metric satisfies:
   $$g_{\mu\nu}^{\mathrm{FS}} = 4\operatorname{Re}\!\left[\langle\partial_\mu\psi|\partial_\nu\psi\rangle - \langle\partial_\mu\psi|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|\partial_\nu\psi\rangle\right] = \frac{4m^2}{\hbar^2}\big[\operatorname{Cov}(\pi_\mu,\pi_\nu) + \operatorname{Cov}(u_\mu,u_\nu)\big]_{\mathcal{P}}$$
   which also correctly matches the classical Fisher information in the limit $\pi_\mu = 0$.

Substituting $x = \hbar$ yields $C = \dfrac{4m^2}{x^2}$.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
